purpose: Resolves the ui-ux-accessibility audit findings (issue #288): replaces confidence-mapped emoji badges with severity-aligned badges plus explicit screen-reader-safe confidence text, adds progress/failure feedback comments to the Probot review/audit/reply paths, consolidates the triplicated badge/bullet rendering into shared helpers, and swaps hash-derived/hardcoded label colors for a WCAG-AA-verified semantic palette on GitHub and GitLab.
riskRationale: Changes are confined to markdown rendering helpers and best-effort status-comment posting; build, typecheck, lint, and the full 757-test suite pass, and the WCAG contrast claims are empirically verified. Remaining findings are UX gaps in edge paths (a review status marker that can stay stale, audit failure feedback not reaching the live path, an unsanitized audit error string) with no security, correctness, or data-integrity regressions.

text: A well-scoped, well-tested PR that cleanly resolves the audit findings: the triplicated getConfidenceBadge logic (which showed a confidence emoji ahead of the severity label, violating WCAG 1.4.1) is consolidated into severity-aligned shared helpers, the new label palette is deterministically contrast-safe and verified by a real WCAG luminance test, and review/audit/reply handlers now surface failures instead of silently no-opping. The main gaps are that the new '⏳ Reviewing this PR...' status marker is left permanently stuck on the empty-result and postReview success:false paths, the audit failure feedback is not wired into the live /audit subscriber and posts an unsanitized error string, and non-severity labels silently lose their distinct colors.

reasoning: The core fixes are correct and well-tested, but three important issues remain before merge: the review-in-progress marker is never resolved to a terminal state when the engine returns empty content or postReview returns {success:false} without throwing (pr-review.ts:128,167); the audit failure feedback is dead code on the live path because the registered auditSubscriber in app/src/index.ts:171 does not thread issueNumber and several audit early-return paths still no-op silently; and the audit failure comment posts a raw, unsanitized error where pr-review.ts correctly uses sanitizeErrorMessage. All are small, well-understood fixes matching patterns already present in this PR.

message: formatIssueBullet provides a single canonical renderer, eliminating the triplicated getConfidenceBadge copies in jsonl-parser.ts, autofix-body.ts, and review-body.ts. The severity-aligned badge now agrees with the bolded severity text (directly resolving the WCAG 1.4.1 color-only contradiction), and formatConfidenceLabel appends explicit '[low/medium confidence]' text that is screen-reader-safe. The deleted test-only buildReviewBody in jsonl-parser.ts was indeed consumed only by tests, so the cleanup is safe.

The accessibility claim is genuinely verified: the test computes WCAG relative luminance and asserts each palette color meets the 4.5:1 AA ratio against white text (measured 7.0/5.47/6.91/4.55:1), replacing the old GitLab hardcoded #6699cc which only achieved ~3.0:1, and the adapter tests assert the semantic color reaches the API on both platforms.

Engine and postReview failure messages posted to PR threads go through sanitizeErrorMessage (message-only, token-redacted) rather than raw error strings or stack traces, avoiding internal path disclosure and secret leakage in public-facing comments.

The marker-prefixed '⏳ Reviewing this PR...' comment mirrors the autofix loop's postOrUpdateComment pattern, so progress and failure updates overwrite a single comment instead of accumulating spam, and the status post is wrapped in its own try/catch so a transient comment failure cannot abort the review.

The new '⏳ Reviewing this PR...' status marker is never resolved to a terminal state on two non-throwing paths, leaving a permanently stale in-progress comment that contradicts the very progress-feedback fix this PR delivers. (1) When the engine returns no meaningful content (lines 128-131), the handler warns and returns null without updating the marker. (2) When gh.postReview resolves with {success:false} instead of throwing — both GitHubHelper.postReview (github.ts:628-631) and GitLabAdapter.postReview (gitlab-adapter.ts:503-506) do this on API rejection — the else branch at lines 167-169 only logs a warning, so the marker stays at '⏳' forever.
suggestion: Update the marker to a terminal state in both non-exception paths before returning: post a neutral completion message in the empty-result branch and a failure message in the reviewResult.success===false branch, both wrapped in the same try/catch-with-warn pattern used elsewhere in the file.

message: The audit silent-failure fix is ineffective on the live /audit path. The updated app/src/subscribers/audit.ts threads issueNumber into handleAudit, but that file is never wired in: app/src/index.ts registers its own inline auditSubscriber (index.ts:160-178) which still calls handleAudit(event.repo || '', getToken(), config) without the issue number, and registerSubscribers() from subscribers/index.ts is never imported (package main -> dist/index.js). Engine failures on the live /audit path therefore still no-op silently, and the earlier no-output returns in handleAudit (prompts dir missing, no prompt files, prompt not found, prompt read failure, empty result at audit.ts:54-107/140) post no user feedback either.
suggestion: Thread the triggering issue/PR number into handleAudit from the live inline auditSubscriber in app/src/index.ts (mirroring the updated subscribers/audit.ts and commands.ts), and post the '<!-- audit-error -->' comment from the early-return paths as well so a user-triggered /audit always gets feedback.

message: The audit failure comment interpolates the raw err.message (or String(err)) into a public issue/PR thread without sanitizeErrorMessage, whereas the same PR's review-failure comments (pr-review.ts:118,144) wrap the message in sanitizeErrorMessage. Engine/OpenCode error strings can embed local paths, request internals, or tokens (GitHub/OpenAI/Anthropic), which would then be visible to anyone who can read the repo's issues — an inconsistency that leaks more than the review path.
suggestion: Import sanitizeErrorMessage from '@opencode-pr-agent/lib' and wrap the error before interpolating it into the failure comment, matching pr-review.ts (message-only, token-redacted output).

message: getSeverityBadge has no default case (the deleted getConfidenceBadge had one), so an out-of-union severity value at runtime would render the literal string 'undefined' in user-facing bullets via formatIssueBullet/buildInlineComments. TypeScript's exhaustiveness currently guards this since Severity is a closed union, so this is defensive hardening rather than a live bug.
suggestion: Add a default fallback returning a neutral known badge (e.g. '⚪') so rendering can never emit 'undefined' as the Severity union evolves.

message: getLabelColor returns a single neutral gray (6e7781) for every non-severity label. The previous hash-based generateLabelColor produced a distinct deterministic color per label, so audit:<category> labels (audit:security-privacy, audit:error-handling-resilience, etc.) and the autofix labels will now all render as identical gray — a silent scannability regression in label-heavy repos that was outside the scope of the severity-label fix.
suggestion: Keep the semantic palette for the three severity labels but preserve distinct, contrast-safe colors for other labels by mapping the name hash onto a small palette of pre-verified accessible colors, with gray as the ultimate fallback.

message: ensureLabels only POSTs new labels; creating a label that already exists returns 422, which is caught and swallowed (core.debug). Labels created by earlier versions (hash-derived HSL on GitHub, hardcoded #6699cc on GitLab) therefore keep their old colors, so the WCAG-AA semantic palette only takes effect on brand-new repositories and existing installs never pick up the corrected label colors.
suggestion: On a 422 for an existing label, PATCH it to update its color to getLabelColor(name) (with a '#' prefix on GitLab) instead of swallowing the error, or document a one-time manual re-color for existing repos.

message: On GitLab, the new progress/failure comments go through postOrUpdateComment, which targets /issues/:iid/notes (gitlab-adapter.ts:585-621). Merge requests use /merge_requests/:iid/notes, so for a GitLab MR the review-in-progress/failure marker posts will 404 and be silently swallowed by the catch — the status feedback fix never reaches GitLab MRs.
suggestion: Route status/failure comments through an MR-aware comment path when the platform is GitLab (or have the GitLab adapter's postOrUpdateComment fall back to /merge_requests/:iid/notes when the issues endpoint 404s).

message: In the no-output branch, the failure reply is posted without its own try/catch. If replyToReviewComment throws there (e.g. a network drop where the POST was received but the response was lost), control falls through to the outer catch at line 73, which posts a second, differently-worded failure reply — a user can receive two conflicting error messages on the same thread.
suggestion: Wrap the failure-reply post inside the no-output branch in its own try/catch so a failed failure-reply does not trigger the generic catch-block reply, or return a sentinel to distinguish it in the outer catch.

message: This smoke-test script destructures buildReviewBody from './lib/jsonl-parser' (line 49) and calls it on line 65, but buildReviewBody was removed from lib/src/jsonl-parser.ts in this PR (it now lives in lib/src/utils/review-body.ts). The script is not wired into CI and its require path was already unresolvable, but it should be updated or removed rather than left referencing a function that no longer exists there.
suggestion: Update the script to require buildReviewBody from the compiled package export (lib/src/utils/review-body.js) or delete the legacy script.

message: The headline behavioral changes — the review-in-progress/complete status comments, the audit failure comment and issueNumber threading, and the reply failure-reply path — have no automated tests. The lib helper changes are well covered, but the app handlers are the riskiest part of this PR and none of the new marker/comment logic is exercised by a test.
suggestion: Add a test setup for the app package (or a thin unit wrapper around the marker/comment logic) asserting the status marker is posted before the engine run, resolved to '✅ Review complete' on success, replaced with a failure message on throw, and that handleAudit only posts the failure comment when issueNumber is defined.
